hints.title: Manhattan Target Distance
hints.text: The minimum moves to reach (targetX, targetY) depends on the total Manhattan distance abs(x) + abs(y).

hints.title: Triangular Sum Bound
hints.text: Find the smallest step count n such that the triangular sum n * (n + 1) / 2 is at least the target distance.

hints.title: Parity Matching Condition
hints.text: Reversing an intermediate move changes the total sum by an even quantity, requiring (total - s) to be even.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minMoves(self, targetX: int, targetY: int) -> int:
        # Move step k has length 2^(k-1) or step size k
        # Target coordinate absolute distances
        x = abs(targetX)
        y = abs(targetY)
        s = x + y
        if s == 0:
            return 0
        # Minimal steps n where n*(n+1)//2 >= s and (n*(n+1)//2 - s) % 2 == 0
        n = 0
        total = 0
        while total < s or (total - s) % 2 != 0:
            n += 1
            total += n
        return n
```

complexity.notes: Triangular step sum progression and parity check in sub-linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating all step combinations in grid directions causes exponential branching.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pure mathematical formulation uses constant memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use Manhattan distance and parity of triangular numbers to find minimum steps.
